title: Beans, kidney, dark red, canned, sodium added, sugar added, drained and rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Dark red kidney beans in cans are cooked beans that have been hot‑processed, with added salt and a small amount of sugar. After being drained, the beans are usually rinsed to remove excess brine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kidney beans are named for their kidney‑shaped seeds.
The deep red color comes from anthocyanins, natural antioxidants.
Canning allows the beans to be stored for several years while retaining most nutrients.
Kidney beans are a staple in Mediterranean, Latin American, and Southeast Asian cuisines.
Sugar is added to balance flavor and improve texture.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: One cup provides about 15 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Contains iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and potassium, important for blood formation, nerve function, and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact after rinsing
items.content: Removing part of the brine reduces sodium and slows carbohydrate absorption.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned beans often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Present in legumes and can reduce mineral absorption; rinsing lowers its level.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans can cause bloating and flatulence in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the beans to salads, soups, stews, chili, or use them as fillings for vegetables and tortillas. Before use, rinse them under cold water to remove excess brine, then heat on the stove or in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. Once opened, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 4‑5 days. Discard if they develop an off‑odor or discoloration.
